L12·N7627unmasked layer
This neuron fires on the delimiter that closes an item in an enumeration or appositive/descriptive phrase — commas between list items ("iPad,", "family,"), the "and" before the final item, place-name commas ("COUNTY, Fla"), and the period/closing-paren-period ending a parenthetical credential or descriptor — i.e., it is a list/appositive-boundary punctuation detector rather than a semantic feature (plain sentence-final periods after ordinary clauses push it negative).

L18·N6086unmasked layer
This neuron is weakly polysemantic and mostly defined by its negative pole: it is strongly *suppressed* by connective function words ("and", "To", "For") inside list-like/title-like enumerations, while its positive activations are scattered on relatively unpredictable content-ish tokens at boundaries — a semicolon, a newline after a sentence, a proper name after a quote ("Sherlock"), a digit, or a word-fragment in an email address.

L23·N11224unmasked layer
Low-specificity contextual neuron that peaks on the "hinge" token right before a named entity or appositive continuation in flowing descriptive/journalistic prose — e.g., the comma after a noun phrase, the dash before a person's name, "artist" before the name, "for" before the team, "Air" inside "Los Angeles Air Force Base", or the newline separating speaker turns — rather than on any single lexical item.
